chunks: I said to Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him): Our city is a cold city, so what do you say regarding wearing this fur? He said: Wear from it what can be eaten (permissible animals) and is guaranteed (properly slaughtered).

key_terms.أُكِلَ: That which is eaten — a legal criterion indicating the animal is from a halal species
key_terms.الوبر: Fur, camel hair, or the hair/coat of an animal — here referring to animal fur used in clothing
key_terms.ضُمِنَ: Guaranteed, secured — here referring to proper Islamic slaughter (dhabh), ensuring permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islam to wear fur from animals?
ai.summary: Abu Tamamah asked Imam al-Jawad (peace be upon him) about the permissibility of wearing fur given the cold climate of his city. The Imam responded with a concise jurisprudential principle: one may wear fur only from animals that are both halal (permissible to eat) and properly slaughtered (dhabh). This ruling reflects the broader Islamic principle that the permissibility of animal by-products (wool, fur, hair) follows the same criteria as the permissibility of the animal's flesh.
